t: Kairouan was founded around 670 as an Arab military post far from the sea, and under the Aghlabids (800 to 909) it became a capital and a centre of Islamic and secular learning.
The Fatimids neglected it after 909 and the Zirids ruled again from it, until the Banu Hilal and Banu Sulaym took it in 1057 and ended its standing as the leading city of Ifriqiya.
The city began to recover under the Hafsids in the 13th century, was taken by the French in 1881, and kept its Great Mosque, its basins and its place in Islamic tradition.
dyk: Local tradition holds that seven pilgrimages to the Great Mosque of Kairouan equal one pilgrimage to Mecca, and according to some this makes it the fourth holiest city in Islam.
ev: Uqba ibn Nafi chooses the site of Kairouan for a military post
The Berber leader Al-Kahina is killed and her army defeated
Handhala ibn Safwan defeats the great Berber army near the city
Ibrahim ibn al-Aghlab becomes emir of Ifriqiya and makes Kairouan his capital
The Fatimids overthrow the Aghlabids and neglect Kairouan
The Banu Hilal take Kairouan from the Zirids and destroy it
Under the Hafsids the city begins to emerge from its ruins
The French take Kairouan and open it to non-Muslims

f.founded: Around 670, when the Arab general Uqba ibn Nafi, acting for Caliph Mu'awiya, chose the site for a military post; a Byzantine garrison town, Kamounia, had stood there before the Arab conquest.
f.where: On a plain inland in central Tunisia, 50 km from the east coast, west of Sousse and 184 km from Tunis.
f.known: A military foundation of the Arab conquest; capital of the Aghlabids; the Great Mosque and its teaching; Maliki scholarship; a Jewish centre of Talmudic learning; the Aghlabid basins; destruction by the Banu Hilal in 1057
f.today: Kairouan is the capital of the Kairouan Governorate in Tunisia, and its old city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
